newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cancer is second biggest killer disease in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Cancer is second biggest killer disease in Brazil.

text.p: Cancer continues to be the second leading cause of death by illness in Brazil with an estimated 97,705 deaths expected in 1997, according to figures published on Tuesday by the National Cancer Institute (INCA).
INCA expects a total of 248,355 new cases of cancer to be diagnosed in Brazil in 1997, of which 52,540 will be fatal in men and 45,165 in women. Brazil has a population of approximately 160 million.

"This means there will be a slight increase (in the number of cancer deaths) in comparison with last year which follows more or less the life expectancy curve or the increase in average life expectancy. As we live longer the risk of getting cancer rises," INCA Director Marcos Moraes said.
Lung cancer causes the largest number of cancer deaths in Brazil overall and among men, but breast cancer is the biggest killer among women and the third leading cause of cancer deaths overall.

"The figures are not alarming, they are comparable with those in other countries, but people should realise that the majority of causes of cancer derive from our lifestyles," Moraes said. "They are causes which can be avoided like smoking and poor eating habits."

Stomach cancer, the second leading cause of cancer deaths overall in Brazil, is on the decline as standards of living and people's diets improve, while prostate cancer is increasing as people live longer, Moraes said.
The leading cause of death by illness in Brazil is heart disease.
